unresolved_should_improve.claim: The revision cuts two things the first draft kept. One is the opening of source P11, which says these impressions are felt in violent emotion by a mind different from the reasoning one. The other is source P10's commonplaces of religion and poetry and the Society-immortal / Adams-mortal antithesis. The vision of shapeless energies now stands as unframed assertion. 'The usual anodynes' no longer echoes the commonplaces that failed.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: 'Phantasm, a nightmare, an insanity of force' and Mont Blanc 'for a moment' still mark the vision as subjective.

evidence.quote: Impressions like these are not reasoned or catalogued in the mind; they are felt as part of violent emotion
knew by heart the thousand commonplaces of religion and poetry which seemed to deaden one's senses and veil the horror
Impressions like these are not reasoned or catalogued in the mind; they are felt as part of violent emotion
The first serious consciousness of Nature's gesture--her attitude towards life--took form then as a phantasm, a nightmare, an insanity of force.
Death took features altogether new to him, in these rich and sensuous surroundings.

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Restore the first clause of source P11 ('Impressions like these are not reasoned... violent emotion') before 'The first serious consciousness'. Optionally restore 'Society being immortal... felt only the mortality.'
unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: Required. It bears on dependency 3 and the essential 'collapse of the stage-scenery of the senses'.
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: The nightmare reads more like a reasoned cosmology. That pulls it toward the later chaos theory, which the plan says must not be imported. The logic leading to Stoicism and atheism-as-comfort is also weakened.
unresolved_should_improve.title: Death passage loses its emotion-not-reason frame and the commonplaces that set up the anodynes

unresolved_should_improve.claim: The first draft kept the sentence saying the American never cared for money or power once earned. The revision cut it. 'Jim Fisk alone seemed to know what he wanted' now follows 'awed by money', so it is unclear what Fisk wanted.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: 'Awed by money' gives a faint thematic link.

evidence.quote: he had no use for wealth. Jim Fisk alone seemed to know what he wanted; Jay Gould never did.
Work and whiskey were his stimulants; but he never cared much for money or power after he earned them.
distrustful of himself, and awed by money. Jim Fisk alone seemed to know what he wanted; Jay Gould never did.

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Restore 'but he never cared much for money or power after he earned them' before the Fisk line, or cut the Fisk/Gould sentence.
unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: Optional paragraph 26. The authorized cut leaves a dangling residue.
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: The plan says to keep the Fisk/Gould contrast or cut it whole. A residue remains whose joke depends on a removed premise.
unresolved_should_improve.title: Fisk/Gould contrast left without its premise

unresolved_should_improve.claim: The first draft had already dropped 'What he could gain at Harvard College he did not know'. The revision also drops 'He thought it a mistake; but his opinion did not prove that it was one...'. 'What he lost at Washington' now has no paired counterpart. Adams's characteristic doubt about his own judgment is gone.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: 'He never could make up his mind whether they were right or not' keeps some uncertainty.

evidence.quote: He thought it a mistake; but his opinion did not prove that it was one, since, in all probability, whatever he did would be more or less a mistake.
What he could gain at Harvard College he did not know, but in any case it was nothing he wanted.
He thought it a mistake; but his opinion did not prove that it was one
he never could make up his mind whether they were right or not. What he lost at Washington he could partly see, but in any case it was not fortune.

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Restore the 'He thought it a mistake...' sentence and the 'What he could gain at Harvard...' sentence before the Washington line.
unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: Bears on the essential 'break at twenty-four hours' notice' and the voice profile's hedging.
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: The break reads as a simple grievance rather than the ironic 'cross-roads of education which all led astray'.
unresolved_should_improve.title: Adams's self-undercutting hedge on the Harvard decision removed

unresolved_should_improve.claim: The first draft kept two passages that the revision cuts. One shows Gladstone, Napoleon and Bismarck as astounded as Adams. The other is the closing question about people smiling at his Paris 'dotage'.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: 'Within three months, his world was to be upset' still pays off the irony. The paragraph ends strongly on the American-regiments contrast.

evidence.quote: How could Adams prophesy that in another year or two, when he spoke of his Paris and its tastes, people would smile at his dotage?
Mr. Gladstone was as much astounded as Adams; the Emperor Napoleon was nearly as stupefied as either
On July 4, all Europe had been in peace; on July 14, Europe was in full chaos of war. As education, the outbreak of the war was wholly lost

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Restore the Gladstone/Napoleon/Bismarck sentence after the July dates. Optionally restore the 'dotage' question as the paragraph's close.
unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: Bears on the essential Palgrave irony. Paragraph 13 lineage material may shrink, but these lines are not lineage.
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: Palgrave's prediction and Adams's dismissal lose their wry closure: the line showing nobody foresaw the war is gone. The elderly narrator's retrospective irony over Paris also disappears.
unresolved_should_improve.title: War section loses universal stupefaction and the retrospective 'dotage' close

unresolved_should_improve.claim: Without 'After waiting ten or a dozen years for some one to show consciousness of his existence', the Terebratula has no point of comparison. The fixed, unnoticed creature is meant to mirror Adams's long neglect.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: Chapter 017's revision establishes the Terebratula as an unchanging type.
